intent: To illustrate public opinion poll results regarding the preferred direction of house prices in Britain.

units.meaning: The Rise option is the least chosen answer, with only 7% saying rising prices would be good for Britain.

basis.note: Table value for Rise; the minimum among the four options.

accepted_routes: Only 7% say rising house prices would be good for Britain
Just 7% choose the Rise option
Rise is the smallest group at 7%
7% favour prices continuing to rise
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Rise bar must be visible with its 7% value label and must read as the shortest/lowest option.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'With polls now showing only 7 % think it'd be good for Britain if prices keep rising'
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly state the 7% Rise figure, or is a clearly shortest Rise bar sufficient?

units.meaning: Fall is the most common answer, at 42%.

basis.note: Table value for Fall; the maximum among the four options.

accepted_routes: Fall leads the poll at 42%
42% prefer falling house prices
The largest group, 42%, says prices should fall
Fall is the top answer with 42%
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Fall bar must be visible, labelled 42%, and must read as the tallest/highest option.
units.temporal_anchor: the poll-results reveal around 'polls now showing ...' (the main result clause)
units.reviewer_question: Must the video identify Fall as the most chosen answer at 42%, even though the provided narration only cites Rise?

units.meaning: The full rank order from most to least chosen is Fall (42%), Stay (29%), Unsure (22%), Rise (7%).
accepted_routes: Order from most to least: Fall, Stay, Unsure, Rise
Fall > Stay > Unsure > Rise
The ranking is Fall (42%), Stay (29%), Unsure (22%), Rise (7%)
Fall first, then Stay, then Unsure, then Rise
units.visual_evidence_rule: All four category bars/labels must be visible in a way that lets the viewer infer the descending order Fall, Stay, Unsure, Rise.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show all four categories in rank order, or can it omit the middle categories?

units.meaning: Fall is far larger than Rise: 42% versus 7%, a gap of 35 percentage points, or six times as large.
accepted_routes: Fall is 35 points above Rise (42% vs 7%)
Fall is six times as common as Rise
Rise is only one-sixth the size of Fall
The Fall-vs-Rise gap is 35 percentage points
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both Fall (42%) and Rise (7%) bars/labels must be visible together so the gap or ratio can be computed.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'polls now showing only 7 %...' clause, if extended into a direct Fall-vs-Rise comparison
units.reviewer_question: Should the video include the derived Fall-vs-Rise gap/ratio, or is that optional enrichment?

units.meaning: The poll responses form a 42% Fall, 29% Stay, 22% Unsure, 7% Rise split, totaling 100%.
accepted_routes: The poll splits 42% Fall, 29% Stay, 22% Unsure, 7% Rise
The four answers total 100%
Responses are 42/29/22/7 shares of the poll
Together the categories account for 100%
units.visual_evidence_rule: All four category labels and values must be visible, with a total or 100% indicator/callout showing they make up the whole poll.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video communicate that the four percentages sum to 100% of the poll, rather than just showing separate bar values?

optional_valid: A separate Stay callout at 29% as the second-most common answer.
A separate Unsure callout at 22% as the third-most common answer.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for why only 7% think rising prices are good.
Extrapolating future house-price direction or predicting what will happen.
Claiming the percentages are shares of the whole British adult population rather than poll respondents.
Values not in the table, such as 50%, 61%, or 43%.
Comparisons to previous polls without additional data.
notes: All cited percentages come from the bar_86 value column; derived totals use 42+29+22+7=100 and 42-7=35 / 42/7=6. The table does not supply a sample size, so the video should not invent one.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
